claims.claim_vi: The source names four pillars of object-oriented programming (abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism), each with a short definition and example; the lesson keeps the four names and order, not the definitions or examples.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: MDN: abstraction reduces complexity by hiding technical complexity behind simpler interfaces; advantages include avoiding low-level code and duplication and changing the internal implementation without affecting the user.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: encapsulation is packing data and functions into one component, for example a class, and controlling access to it so the object is a black box whose users know only its interface.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: inheritance is a major OOP feature; classes can have superclasses and subclasses, the developer chooses which attributes and methods of the superclass to keep and adds their own; some languages allow multiple inheritance.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: polymorphism is the presentation of one interface for multiple data types; in OOP each class is responsible for its own code and data, so each class has its own function that behaves properly for any object.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python tutorial: derived classes may override methods of their base classes; all methods in Python are effectively virtual.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python tutorial: "private" instance variables that cannot be accessed except from inside an object do not exist in Python; a name prefixed with an underscore is treated by convention as non-public; name mangling gives limited support for class-private members.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: The Python abc module provides the infrastructure for defining abstract base classes.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

design_notes_vi: Hai nhóm thẻ (che bớt chi tiết; dùng lại và thay đổi) và một khung ghi nhớ. Lời giải thích từ MDN và tài liệu Python; ví dụ Shape do bài tự nghĩ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source is four short paragraphs with an example for three of the pillars; the lesson keeps the four names and their order, explains each from MDN and the Python documentation, replaces the source's Vehicle and Car examples with its own Shape example and does not use the source image.
Python behavior is not in the source and comes from the pinned CPython documentation; the lesson notes that access modifiers belong to some languages and Python relies on convention.
